flashcard_questions.q: How long should a thorough warm up last?
Which acronym gives the four key components of a warm up?
What does the P in PRMS stand for?
What does the R in PRMS stand for?
What does the M in PRMS stand for?
What does the S in PRMS stand for?
Why does a pulse raiser increase the heart rate?
flashcard_questions.a: To pump more oxygenated blood to the working muscles.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of stretching uses controlled movements such as lunges and leg swings?
How long is a static stretch held?
Which part of a session should static stretching be saved for?
Which stretching technique needs a trained partner and is the most effective?
flashcard_questions.a: PNF stretching, or proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation.

flashcard_questions.q: What is pliability in ligaments and tendons?
flashcard_questions.a: Their ability to stretch and flex without tearing.

flashcard_questions.q: What is skill rehearsal in a warm up?
flashcard_questions.a: Practising movements and techniques from the sport about to be played.

flashcard_questions.q: How does warming the muscles improve reaction time and power?
flashcard_questions.a: Nerve impulses travel faster, speeding up muscle contraction.

flashcard_questions.q: Which psychological benefit comes from following a familiar warm up routine?

notes: 15 cards: 1 acronym plus 4 single-letter PRMS expansions, 3 value cards (15-20 min, 15-30 s), 4 term-to-definition, 3 cause-and-effect. Rugby worked-example timings dropped as illustration.
